evals.query: In my Kora 2.0 service I need a job that runs every day at 3 AM to generate a nightly report. How do I schedule it?
expected_behavior: Adds io.koraframework:scheduling-quartz plus the mandatory processor (annotation-processors for Java, symbol-processors via ksp for Kotlin) under the io.koraframework:kora-bom BOM
Extends the @KoraApp interface with io.koraframework.scheduling.quartz.QuartzModule
Annotates a method on a graph component with @ScheduleQuartzWithCron("0 0 3 * * ?") imported from io.koraframework.scheduling.quartz.annotation
Uses a Quartz cron with 6 or 7 fields and '?' in exactly one of day-of-month / day-of-week, and notes the literal is validated at compile time
Does not emit ru.tinkoff.kora imports, kora-parent, a Spring-style @Scheduled, or field injection
anti_behavior: Imports the RC1-era io.koraframework.scheduling.quartz.ScheduleWithCron
Writes `0 0 3 * * *` without a '?'

expected_behavior: Identifies that the trigger annotation's value() is Class<?> in Kora 2.0, so the nested @Tag form no longer compiles
Rewrites it as @ScheduleQuartzWithTrigger(TriggerScheduler.class) from io.koraframework.scheduling.quartz.annotation — the class tag passed directly, under the current annotation name
Explains the class becomes a @Tag on the org.quartz.Trigger parameter of the generated factory method, so the graph must supply @Tag(TriggerScheduler.class) Trigger
Shows the Trigger declared on the @KoraApp interface with io.koraframework.common.annotation.Tag
Does not suggest a string name, does not suggest keeping @Tag nested, and does not invent a value/tag attribute pair

evals.query: Kotlin, Kora 2.0. My KSP build fails on @ScheduleWithTrigger(Tag(ReportJob::class)) fun schedule() {} inside class ReportJob, ported from Kora 1.x. How should this look now?
expected_behavior: Rewrites it as @ScheduleQuartzWithTrigger(ReportJob::class) — a KClass, not a nested Tag(...)
Shows the matching @Tag(ReportJob::class) fun reportTrigger(): Trigger on the @KoraApp interface
Uses io.koraframework.scheduling.quartz.annotation.ScheduleQuartzWithTrigger and io.koraframework.common.annotation.Tag
Does not claim the class or function must be open — scheduling generates a separate job wrapper, not an AOP proxy
Does not carry ru.tinkoff.kora imports into the fix
States that `open` is NOT required for scheduling: Kora generates a separate $CleanupJob_cleanup_Job wrapper that calls the component directly, so a plain non-open class is correct
Notes that `open` is only needed when a method-wrapping aspect such as @Log, @Retryable or @Timeout is stacked on the same class

Directs the diagnosis at the real silent causes instead: QuartzModule missing from the @KoraApp interface, the KSP processor (io.koraframework:symbol-processors) not applied, the class not being a graph component, or enabled = false under the job's config path
Checks that the annotation is io.koraframework.scheduling.quartz.annotation.ScheduleQuartzWithCron (each scheduler now has its own annotation name)
Does not tell the user to add `open` as the fix

evals.query: Kora 2.0 Kotlin. I want my Quartz cron job to call two suspend repositories in parallel, so I wrote `@ScheduleQuartzWithCron("0 0 * * * ?") suspend fun refresh()`. KSP fails the build. What is the right shape?
expected_behavior: Explains that suspend is rejected by the scheduling symbol processor: Kora 2.0 contracts are synchronous and the error says 'Suspend methods are not supported by the scheduling generator'
Removes suspend and makes the scheduled function a plain function returning Unit
For real parallelism points at java.util.concurrent.StructuredTaskScope (a preview API requiring --enable-preview), as the processor's own message does
Does not suggest runBlocking as the recommended shape, and does not suggest Mono, Flux or CompletionStage — none are Kora 2.0 contracts
Does not reference Context, which no longer exists in the framework

evals.query: I want the cron schedule of my Kora 2.0 Quartz job to be configurable in application.conf instead of hardcoded in the annotation.
expected_behavior: Uses @ScheduleQuartzWithCron(config = "jobs.nightly") and points config at a HOCON node
Shows the node as either a bare string or an object with `cron` (and optionally `enabled` and `telemetry`)
Explains that the config node wins over the annotation `value`, and that with no `value` the node is required — an absent one fails the graph build with ConfigValueException
Mentions that `enabled = false` in the object form registers the job without triggers, and that a cron from config is validated at graph init rather than at compile time
Mentions that per-job telemetry overrides are only available through the config form
Does not invent an annotation attribute such as cron =, expression = or timezone =
Identifies both keys as Kora 1.x paths that Kora 2.0 does not read, and that unknown HOCON keys are ignored without a warning — hence the green but wrong startup
Moves the Quartz properties to scheduling.quartz.properties { "org.quartz.threadPool.threadCount" = "30" }, read by QuartzModule.quartzProperties
Replaces the shutdown flag with scheduling.quartz.shutdownWait (a duration, default 30s): waitForJobComplete is not read anywhere in the current module, under either path
Notes the effective defaults that were silently in force instead: SimpleThreadPool with threadCount 10 and RAMJobStore, from the quartz.properties bundled in the Quartz jar
Does not claim the old keys still work, does not move the flag to scheduling.quartz.waitForJobComplete, and does not invent a `quartz.properties` or `scheduling.quartz.threadCount` key

evals.query: I need a Quartz job in my Kora 2.0 app that fires every 5 seconds using a custom Trigger rather than a cron expression.
expected_behavior: Declares an org.quartz.Trigger built with TriggerBuilder and SimpleScheduleBuilder as a @Tag(SomeClass.class) factory method on the @KoraApp interface
Annotates the job method with @ScheduleQuartzWithTrigger(SomeClass.class) from io.koraframework.scheduling.quartz.annotation using the same class
Explains that the class is a tag on the generated factory method's Trigger parameter, and that a missing tagged Trigger is a DI graph failure
Places the job method on a graph component and keeps it synchronous
Does not use the 1.x nested @Tag(...) form and does not pass a string

evals.query: My hourly Quartz job in Kora 2.0 sometimes runs longer than an hour and I get two overlapping executions. How do I prevent that?
expected_behavior: Adds @DisallowConcurrentExecution from io.koraframework.scheduling.quartz.annotation on the method, next to @ScheduleQuartzWithCron
Notes it is Kora's own annotation read on the method, while org.quartz.DisallowConcurrentExecution is read on the class — the two placements are not interchangeable
Explains the generated job class ends up carrying org.quartz.DisallowConcurrentExecution either way
Optionally mentions bounding the job body, since shutdown waits scheduling.quartz.shutdownWait (30s) and then interrupts a long run
Does not propose a manual lock as the primary solution

evals.query: I just need to run a cleanup task every 30 seconds in my Kora 2.0 service. Should I use Quartz for that?
expected_behavior: Recommends the lighter scheduling-jdk module with @ScheduleJdkAtFixedRate or @ScheduleJdkWithFixedDelay from io.koraframework.scheduling.jdk.annotation
Explains Quartz earns its place for custom org.quartz.Trigger instances, misfire policies, JobExecutionContext/JobDataMap, or a persistent/clustered job store
Notes that each scheduler has its own annotation names (@ScheduleJdkWithCron, @ScheduleQuartzWithCron, @ScheduleDbWithCron), so the annotation decides which scheduler runs the job
Does not add io.koraframework:scheduling-quartz for a plain fixed interval
Does not reference a non-Kora @Scheduled annotation

evals.query: I want my Kora 2.0 Quartz jobs to survive restarts and run once across three replicas using PostgreSQL. I set org.quartz.jobStore.class = org.quartz.impl.jdbcjobstore.JobStoreTX and org.quartz.jobStore.isClustered = true, and my Kora app already has a JDBC datasource. It still fails at startup. What am I missing?
expected_behavior: Puts the Quartz properties under scheduling.quartz.properties, not a root quartz block
States that Kora's JDBC datasource is not wired into Quartz — Quartz manages its own connections and needs an org.quartz.dataSource.<name>.* block with driver, URL, user and password

Points out the application must add a Quartz connection provider itself: HikariCP for org.quartz.utils.HikariCpPoolingConnectionProvider or c3p0 for C3p0PoolingConnectionProvider, because both are provided-scope in the Quartz POM and excluded by scheduling-quartz's build
Requires the QRTZ_* tables to be created from Quartz's DDL; Kora ships no migration for them
Notes instanceName must be identical across replicas while instanceId must differ (Kora already defaults them to kora-quartz-scheduler and AUTO)
Notes every replica must run the same build, because job instances are resolved from the DI graph by the generated job class and Quartz's fallback factory cannot construct one
Does not claim RAMJobStore (the default) persists or clusters

Explains that KoraQuartzScheduler.release() puts the scheduler on standby, waits scheduling.quartz.shutdownWait (default 30s) for running jobs, then interrupts the ones still running through org.quartz.InterruptableJob, which KoraQuartzJob implements, and waits up to shutdownWait once more
Keeps the isInterrupted() check: it is the shutdown signal, and InterruptedException from blocking calls must not be swallowed
Recommends additionally bounding the run below shutdownWait with a deadline or batch cap, and making the job idempotent and resumable

Mentions that 0s interrupts immediately and a large value waits for completion, and that the platform grace period (e.g. Kubernetes terminationGracePeriodSeconds) must cover up to about 2 × shutdownWait
anti_behavior: Claims Quartz or Kora never interrupts a running job on shutdown
Recommends scheduling.quartz.waitForJobComplete or scheduling.waitForJobComplete
Claims Kora jobs cannot implement InterruptableJob

evals.query: Kora 2.0. I enabled Prometheus in my service but no scheduling job metrics show up in /metrics, and I see no job log lines either. Tracing spans do appear. What is wrong?
expected_behavior: Explains that in Kora 2.0 TelemetryConfig defaults logging.enabled and metrics.enabled to false while tracing.enabled defaults to true, which matches exactly what the user observes
Turns them on explicitly under scheduling.telemetry.logging.enabled and scheduling.telemetry.metrics.enabled
Names the metric correctly: a Micrometer Timer scheduling.job.duration

Notes metrics also need a MeterRegistry in the graph, that per-job overrides live under the job's config node and only work for the @ScheduleQuartzWithCron(config = ...) form, and that the timer carries scheduling.system = quartz
Does not claim metrics default to true (that was the Kora 1.x behaviour)

evals.query: Kora 2.0 runs synchronous contracts on virtual threads. Does that mean my Quartz jobs are on virtual threads too, and how many can run at once?
expected_behavior: States that Quartz jobs do not run on Kora's virtual threads: KoraQuartzScheduler builds a plain StdSchedulerFactory, so jobs execute on Quartz's own SimpleThreadPool
Gives the real defaults — platform threads named kora-quartz-scheduler_Worker-N, org.quartz.threadPool.threadCount = 10, non-daemon
Explains threadCount is the ceiling on concurrent executions across all Quartz jobs, and that oversubscribing it delays firings and causes misfires
Shows tuning it via scheduling.quartz.properties { "org.quartz.threadPool.threadCount" = "..." }
Notes Kora still installs its MDC, OpenTelemetry context and scheduling Observation around each execution, so logging and tracing work inside the job body
Does not claim Quartz jobs are virtual threads and does not confuse this with the JDK scheduler's executor

evals.query: Kora 2.0, three replicas, PostgreSQL already in place. A cron job must fire once per hour on exactly one replica and keep its schedule across deploys. We don't need custom triggers or misfire policies. Do I have to set up a clustered Quartz JDBC JobStore?
expected_behavior: Says no: kora-aop-scheduling-db (io.koraframework:scheduling-db-scheduler, DbSchedulerModule) covers this with db-scheduler on one table in the existing database
Uses @ScheduleDbWithCron from io.koraframework.scheduling.db.scheduler.annotation
Keeps Quartz with a clustered JDBC JobStore for needs the DB scheduler lacks: custom org.quartz.Trigger, misfire policies, JobDataMap, L/W/#/C cron
Explains that the JDK scheduler is not an option because every replica runs every job and nothing is persisted
Does not add io.koraframework:scheduling-quartz or Quartz qrtz_* tables for this requirement

evals.query: We built our service against Kora 2.0.0.RC1 and moved to the latest 2.0 build. Now `import io.koraframework.scheduling.quartz.ScheduleWithCron;` and `import io.koraframework.scheduling.quartz.DisallowConcurrentExecution;` fail with 'cannot find symbol'. What changed?
expected_behavior: Explains the Quartz annotations were renamed and moved into io.koraframework.scheduling.quartz.annotation after RC1 (Kora PR #952)

Maps ScheduleWithCron → ScheduleQuartzWithCron and ScheduleWithTrigger → ScheduleQuartzWithTrigger, and moves DisallowConcurrentExecution / PersistJobDataAfterExecution to the .annotation package under the same names
Mentions the silent config change in the same release: scheduling.quartz.waitForJobComplete is gone, replaced by scheduling.quartz.shutdownWait
Mentions that jobs now live in the Quartz group `kora` and that existing DEFAULT-group jobs of known classes are moved automatically
anti_behavior: Suggests downgrading back to RC1 or adding a compatibility dependency
Keeps the flat io.koraframework.scheduling.quartz package for the annotations
Uses the JDK or DB annotation (@ScheduleJdkWithCron / @ScheduleDbWithCron) as the replacement for a Quartz job

evals.query: application.conf of our Kora 2.0 service has `scheduling.quartz.waitForJobComplete = true` so deploys never cut a running Quartz job short. After upgrading Kora a 5-minute job now gets interrupted during shutdown. Why, and how do I keep the old behaviour?
expected_behavior: States waitForJobComplete no longer exists; QuartzConfig reads scheduling.quartz.shutdownWait (duration, default 30s) and the stale key is ignored without a warning

Describes the new shutdown: standby, wait shutdownWait, interrupt still-running jobs via InterruptableJob (WARN 'KoraQuartzScheduler interrupting jobs ... still running after PT30S'), wait shutdownWait again, then shutdown(false)
To wait for completion, sets shutdownWait to a value longer than the longest run (e.g. 10m, or 365d for unbounded) and raises the platform termination grace period to match
Recommends making the job honour Thread.currentThread().isInterrupted() / InterruptedException anyway
anti_behavior: Tells the user to keep or rename waitForJobComplete
Claims the interrupt cannot reach a Kora Quartz job

evals.query: We run Kora Quartz on a JDBC JobStore. Will every application restart reschedule our persisted cron and simple triggers and lose the misfires that happened while the service was down?
expected_behavior: Says no: KoraQuartzJobRegistrar keeps a persisted trigger unless its schedule (cron expression, simple repeat interval/count), end time or cron time zone changed

Explains the start time is ignored by default because a trigger built without startAt() gets a new start time on every build, and comparing it would reschedule every trigger, losing misfire handling and shifting simple-trigger phases
Names scheduling.quartz.compareStartTime (default false) and says to enable it only when every trigger uses a fixed startAt()
Mentions jobs are stored in the Quartz group `kora` under the generated job class's canonical name
anti_behavior: Claims Kora reschedules every persisted trigger on each start
Invents a misfire or reschedule config key other than compareStartTime

evals.query: We deleted a Quartz job class from our Kora 2.0 service that uses a PostgreSQL JobStore. Now every start logs `JobPersistenceException: Couldn't retrieve job because a required class was not found`. How do we get rid of it? We deploy with rolling updates.
expected_behavior: Explains the deleted class's job row stays in the persistent store, so Quartz fails to load it

Names scheduling.quartz.cleanupOrphanedJobs = true (default false), which removes Kora jobs (group `kora`, plus DEFAULT-group jobs named like generated $Type_method_Job classes) the starting instance does not know, before the scheduler starts; jobs added to the Scheduler directly are kept

Warns it is unsafe during a rolling deployment that runs two versions at once (an old instance removes the new version's jobs until a new instance restarts) and when several applications share the Quartz tables under the same scheduler name
Offers the safe alternative for this team: delete the orphaned rows once, or enable the cleanup only for a deploy that does not overlap versions
anti_behavior: Recommends enabling cleanupOrphanedJobs permanently without the rolling-deploy caveat
Invents a different cleanup key

evals.query: After adding a second cron job with `@ScheduleQuartzWithCron(value = "0 0 * * * ?", identity = "hourly")` in another class, our Kora service fails to start with `IllegalStateException: Quartz trigger 'DEFAULT.hourly' is declared more than once, by jobs ...`. What does it want?
expected_behavior: Explains KoraQuartzJobRegistrar checks that trigger identities are unique across all jobs and names both jobs in the error
Fixes it by giving each job a unique identity, or by dropping identity so the default <fully.qualified.Class>#<method> applies, which never collides
Notes the same check covers Trigger beans used with @ScheduleQuartzWithTrigger (TriggerBuilder.withIdentity)
anti_behavior: Suggests catching or ignoring the exception
Claims Quartz silently replaces one of the triggers

evals.query: I put `@ScheduleQuartzWithCron("0 0 * * * ?")` on a method of a component annotated @Conditional(ReportsEnabled.class). With the condition off, the Kora app no longer starts: `Graph node value was not initialized because condition failed: ...`. Isn't the job supposed to disappear with the component?
expected_behavior: Explains the generated Quartz job factory takes the component directly and carries no @Conditional, so the job node still requests the condition-failed component and graph initialisation fails
Says this is fixed in 2.0.0.RC2 (kora-projects/kora PR #962) and only 2.0.0.RC1 is affected; since then the generated job component carries the component's condition
Gives the workaround for builds without it: keep the scheduled method on an unconditional component; if it must call the conditional one, inject All<T> and return when it is empty
Warns against injecting the conditional component as @Nullable, which hits a separate bug (kora-projects/kora PR #960)
anti_behavior: Claims @Conditional on the class already removes its scheduled jobs in current master
Suggests making the component's constructor tolerate the failed condition

evals.query: Our Kora 2.0 pods run in UTC, but the Quartz cron `0 0 9 ? * MON-FRI` must fire at 09:00 Moscow time. Is there a timezone attribute on the annotation?
expected_behavior: Says there is no time-zone attribute on @ScheduleQuartzWithCron

Declares a ZoneId component tagged @Tag(io.koraframework.scheduling.common.SchedulingModule.class), e.g. ZoneId.of("Europe/Moscow"), which every generated cron trigger uses; without it the JVM default zone applies
Notes the component applies to the JDK and DB cron schedulers as well, and that changing it reschedules persisted Quartz cron triggers at the next start
anti_behavior: Invents a timezone/zone annotation attribute or a scheduling.quartz.timeZone key
Only suggests changing the JVM default zone with -Duser.timezone
